_comment: Authored summary targets — plan.md §9. Keyed by dataset record id. Merge with: npm --prefix api run merge:dataset
_batch: 002 — the 16 rules batch-001 did not reach. Completes coverage at 26/26.
red_progressive_deficit-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain with leg pain and weakness for 6 weeks to 3 months, getting worse.

**Key findings**
- Leg or foot weakness worsening quickly, or the foot dragging
- Difficulty standing on toes and heels
- Pain radiates below the knee
- Bladder, bowel and saddle sensation all reported normal
- Walking still unrestricted; painkillers only

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Weakness that is progressing rather than static is what drives the urgency here, independent of a moderate pain score.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- How quickly the weakness has advanced — days or weeks
- Whether the foot catches on steps or uneven ground
- Power by myotome, ankle dorsiflexion in particular
- Whether any bladder change has begun since he filled the form
red_infection-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Fever alongside the back pain
- Pain wakes him at night; sleep disturbed most nights
- Diabetes
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Fever with spinal pain in a diabetic, with night pain on top, raises a query of spinal infection. The severity is high for so short a history.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Temperature, and how long the fever has run
- Any recent skin infection, dental work, injection or IV line
- Percussion tenderness over the spine
- Inflammatory markers and blood cultures before any steroid is given
red_malignancy-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Previously treated for cancer
- Unintentional weight loss
- Pain wakes him at night; sleep disturbed most nights
- Pain stays in the back — no neurological symptoms
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — A cancer history together with night pain and weight loss is the combination that raises a query of metastatic disease.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which primary, when treated, and whether he is still under follow-up
- How much weight, over what period
- Whether the night pain is unrelieved by changing position
- Imaging the whole spine rather than the painful segment alone
red_fracture_trauma-000:
**Snapshot** — 68y man, retired. Lower back pain for under 2 weeks following a fall, 8/10.

**Key findings**
- Recent fall, with the onset dated to it
- Severe pain of very recent onset
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Relieved by lying down; sleep undisturbed
- No imaging yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — A fall at 68 with severe new back pain warrants imaging before the outpatient appointment rather than after it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Mechanism and height of the fall
- Point tenderness over a spinous process
- Whether he could weight-bear immediately afterwards
- Bone health — previous fractures, steroid use, and whether osteoporosis has ever been assessed
amber_motor_deficit-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain with weakness for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Difficulty standing on toes and heels; the leg feels weak
- Pain radiates to the thigh, above the knee
- Weakness reported as static, not rapidly progressing
- Walking unrestricted; no red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Reported motor involvement without rapid progression warrants examination rather than same-day review.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether the weakness is genuine or pain-limited
- Power by myotome, comparing sides
- Whether it has changed at all over the last month
- Reflexes, and any wasting
amber_cervical_radiculopathy-000:
**Snapshot** — 46y woman, teacher. Neck pain with arm pain and numbness for 3 to 12 months, 7/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain radiates below the elbow into the left hand
- Numbness and tingling in the hand and fingers
- No loss of dexterity, no gait disturbance, no bilateral involvement
- Working with difficulty; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Arm pain below the elbow with hand numbness, well beyond six weeks, fits a nerve-root pattern rather than cord involvement.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which fingers, to localise the root
- Spurling's test and upper-limb reflexes
- Whether the arm pain outweighs the neck pain
- Whether resting the hand on her head relieves it
amber_failed_conservative-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year, 6/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- More than six weeks of physiotherapy with no benefit at all
- Work still affected
- Pain stays in the back — no numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- No imaging

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Structured conservative care has been tried for an adequate period and has failed, with function still impaired.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What the physiotherapy involved, and whether he completed it
- Whether it was supervised or a printed exercise sheet
- Whether anything changed the pain at all, even briefly
- What outcome he is hoping for from this consult
amber_functional_collapse-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 8/10, has stopped working.

**Key findings**
- Has had to stop work entirely
- Reports it is still getting worse
- Now needs some help with dressing and bathing
- Sleep disturbed most nights
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation or neurological findings

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Loss of work and continuing deterioration over months, with no neurological cause on the form, is enough on its own to warrant a consult.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What specifically stopped him working, and when
- Whether the deterioration is pain, stiffness, or function
- Mood and sleep, given the duration
- Whether anyone has examined him during this period
grey_shoulder-000:
**Snapshot** — 46y woman, teacher. Neck pain with arm pain for 3 to 12 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Arm pain worse on reaching overhead
- Pain stays above the elbow, at the shoulder only
- No hand numbness, no grip loss, no dexterity change
- Right side; working with difficulty
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Overhead-provoked arm pain that stops above the elbow, with no hand symptoms, points to the shoulder joint rather than a cervical root.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Painful arc, and whether passive movement hurts as much as active
- Impingement tests and rotator cuff power
- Whether the pain wakes her lying on that side
- Whether neck movement changes the arm pain at all
grey_inflammatory-000:
**Snapshot** — 31y man, student. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
- Pain improves with movement and worsens with rest
- Under 45, with months of symptoms
- No radiation, numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Prolonged morning stiffness with exercise-responsive pain, at this age and duration, fits an inflammatory rather than mechanical pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Alternating buttock pain, or heel and chest wall pain
- Personal or family history of psoriasis, uveitis or inflammatory bowel disease
- Whether anti-inflammatories help dramatically, which would support the pattern
- Whether pain wakes him in the second half of the night
grey_widespread-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y woman, desk job. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain in many parts of the body with constant tiredness
- Sleep disturbed most nights
- The back pain itself has no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; managing daily tasks independently
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Widespread pain with persistent fatigue and no localising spinal findings suggests the back pain is one part of a broader picture.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which other sites hurt, and whether they came before or after the back
- Sleep quality separately from pain — unrefreshing sleep is part of the pattern
- Mood, concentration, and how long the fatigue has run
- Whether the fatigue has ever been investigated
green_acute_mechanical-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks after lifting, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Sudden onset after lifting or bending
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation past the thigh
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Rest only so far

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Under six weeks, mechanical onset, no neurological findings and no red flags. This sits inside the natural-history window.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What he lifted, and whether the same load recurs at work
- Whether he has stayed active or rested completely
- What he expects to happen, and what is worrying him
- Whether he knows which symptoms should bring him back sooner
advisory_hip_overlap-000:
**Snapshot** — 61y man, desk job. Lower back and leg pain with numbness for 3 to 12 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain radiates below the knee on the left, with leg numbness
- Groin-dominant pain and hip stiffness also reported
- Two patterns present at once — nerve root and hip
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Below-knee radiation with numbness fits a lumbar nerve-root pattern. The hip findings sit alongside it rather than displacing it.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Whether the groin pain and the leg pain behave differently
- Hip internal rotation, and whether it reproduces the groin pain
- Straight-leg raise, to separate the two
- Which of the two limits him more day to day
advisory_pregnancy-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y woman, homemaker, pregnant. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pregnancy reported — imaging and medication options are restricted
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Taking painkillers, unspecified
- No physiotherapy yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Six weeks or more of uncomplicated back pain, no neurological findings, and structured conservative care not yet attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Gestation, and whether she is under obstetric care
- Exactly which painkillers she has been taking
- Whether pelvic girdle pain describes this better than lumbar pain
- Referral to a physiotherapist experienced in pregnancy
advisory_recent_imaging-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- MRI within the last 3 months; films and report not yet seen
- Pain stays in the back — no numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief
- No physiotherapy yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Months of pain with no neurological findings and no structured conservative care attempted. The existing scan does not change that.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Ask him to bring the films and the full report, not just the conclusion
- Who requested the scan, and what he was told about it
- Whether the report has shaped what he expects from this consult
- Whether physiotherapy was offered after the scan
advisory_free_text-000:
**Snapshot** — 44y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- His note says the pain is worst on waking and eases once he moves
- Yet he answered no to morning stiffness beyond 30 minutes, and no to pain improving with movement
- No radiation, numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy

**Supporting the triage verdict** — On the structured answers this is uncomplicated chronic back pain with conservative care not yet tried.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- His note describes an inflammatory pattern the tick-boxes deny — worth resolving directly
- How long the morning stiffness actually lasts, timed
- Whether movement helps within minutes or hours
- If the note is accurate, an inflammatory cause deserves consideration
